detector: the inverse stale-allowlist assertion in pairing-route-scopes.test.ts
summary: A comment placed between `context.app.route('/api/models',` and `createModelsRoutes` made the whole mount non-matching for pairing-route-leaf-scan's `routeRe`, so four authenticated leaves (GET /api/models, /aws-profiles, /capabilities, /pricing/:modelId) silently left the pairing-scope security scan. The scan reported clean; there was no diagnostic. What caught it was not the coverage assertion but its INVERSE — the stale-allowlist check, which noticed four already-seeded declarations the live scan no longer discovered. A leaf that was new behind such a mount would have had no seeded entry and would have vanished undetected.
fix_ref: station PR #1615 moved the comment above the mount — the instance, not the scanner limitation
notes: Recorded as a machine catch because the assertion genuinely fired and blocked, but the machine that caught it was the one nobody designed for this: coverage passed, staleness failed. The gate's own leaf-count check is `toBeGreaterThan(300)` — a floor, which by construction cannot notice four leaves going missing from 420.

detector: source read of pairing-route-leaf-scan.ts's routeRe, prompted by the #1615 instance
summary: Asking WHY #1615's four leaves disappeared exposed a pre-existing instance on main: runtime-routes.ts mounts /integrations with a comment in the same position, so twelve authenticated leaves — including POST /integrations/:serverId/ui/call, which executes an MCP tool, and POST /integrations/:serverId/ui/permissions — have never once been seen by the leaf-coverage guard. They resolve to a scope at runtime through the generic family split, so nothing is unauthenticated; what is missing is the conscious per-leaf confirmation the guard exists to force. No assertion could see this: they had no seeded allowlist entries to go stale, and 420 leaves is comfortably over the floor of 300.
evidence_ref: station#1634; src-server/runtime/routes/runtime-routes.ts:682 (/integrations mount); the twelve leaves enumerated on that issue
notes: Open. #1555's scope-coverage invariant now pins the gap as an enumerated one (MOUNTS_THE_SCAN_CANNOT_SEE in pairing-route-scopes.test.ts) so a SECOND blind spot cannot hide behind the first, but closing it needs the comment-tolerant regex plus a security judgement on the twelve leaves — both tracked on #1634. Independently reproduced 2026-08-03 while fault-injecting that pin: applying the comment-tolerant regex makes the scan discover exactly those twelve and no others.

detector: implementer fault injection (deleted 'packages' from REFERENCE_ROOTS)
summary: A scope-coverage assertion written for the undefined-CSS-custom-properties guard iterated REFERENCE_ROOTS and asserted each declared root contributed references. It cannot catch the failure it was written for: delete a root and the loop simply iterates one fewer time with every assertion still passing. The injection that removed 'packages' came back GREEN while the guard silently stopped auditing an entire tree — and the pre-existing floor (references > 500) stayed satisfied too, because src-ui/src alone clears it many times over. Replaced with an independent pin of the expected root lists; the same injection then reds.
fix_ref: same branch — 'test(css): pin the declared scan scope independently'; per-root non-emptiness kept alongside the pin, since each catches what the other cannot
notes: A scope assertion derived from the same constant it is checking is self-satisfying by construction. Found only because the slice's own rule was that every fixture must be proven in BOTH directions — one of ten injections in that pass came back green, and the protocol treats an uncaught injection as a stop signal rather than a shrug.

detector: reading the command's own output instead of the sentinel it printed
summary: An `if git commit -q -m ... 2>&1 | tail -20; then echo COMMIT_OK; else ...` wrapper printed COMMIT_OK for a commit that never happened — git exited non-zero on 'no changes added to commit' (a preceding `git add -A` had been refused as part of a rejected compound command), and the `if` read tail's exit, not git's. The stated rule in this repo's own delivery protocol is that the condition must be the real command, never a pipeline; the pipeline had been introduced purely to keep the log readable. Caught immediately because the tail output printed underneath said 'no changes added to commit', which contradicted the sentinel above it.
fix_ref: re-run as `if git commit ... > file 2>&1; then` with the log redirected rather than piped
notes: The fourth recorded instance of a class first written down on 2026-06-12, produced this time by an agent that had read the rule an hour earlier and reintroduced the pipe for readability. The failure mode is not ignorance of the rule; it is that a pipe is the natural way to keep output short.

detector: normalizing and diffing the two occurrence lists instead of the verdict lines
summary: A branch gated red on the state-primitives ratchet at 52 ad-hoc "No X" occurrences. The A/B against main appeared to exonerate main — the branch printed `FAIL: 52 ...` while main appeared to print `OK`. That `OK` was a DIFFERENT check's verdict line (`OK: empty-family count 1 <= ceiling 1`) matched by a loose grep; the ad-hoc check's own verdict was never read. Diffing the normalized occurrence lists settled it: 52 on both, zero new entries, the branch innocent. The obvious next move had the grep been believed was to raise the ceiling to unblock a branch that had added nothing — banking pre-existing debt onto an unrelated change.
evidence_ref: station#1665; scripts/state-primitives-ratchet.mjs (two independent checks, two OK: lines)
fix_ref: station@008b4ead / #1668 — ported the offending views rather than raising the ceiling
notes: A verdict was present and simply not read: the ad-hoc check's own line was never matched, and a neighbouring check's success stood in for it. Filed as misattributed-evidence rather than absence-as-success for that reason — nothing was missing, it was the wrong result read as the right one. Same shape as reading a pipeline's tail instead of the command's exit.

detector: tracing the read path of the gate's own metric on a live install
summary: Slice 3c's gate was "the divergence record is empty AND the shadow-comparison metric shows all four populations were exercised". The metric half cannot be read from a real Station: telemetry.ts starts the OTel NodeSDK only when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set, so with it unset `metrics.getMeter('station')` returns a no-op meter and station.project_resource.shadow_comparisons has been discarding every write since slice 3a merged. Nothing is buffered and there is no in-process read path — no /metrics scrape, no Prometheus or Console exporter, no accessor. The empty divergence record therefore proved nothing: it was the instrument being absent, not the divergence being absent. CONFLATED_UNBOUND_NOTE calls itself a fail-open tripwire that must read zero before 3c flips — a tripwire whose only reader is an optional external collector nobody has attached cannot report that it fired.
evidence_ref: station#1686; src-server/telemetry.ts; docs/patterns/backend.md:537; live install 2026-08-03 (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT unset, zero shadow lines in ~/.station/logs/default.log)
notes: Open; blocks #1501 slice 3c. The issue is explicit that option 1 (a readable local record) should not be built by the lane that also wants to pass the gate. Note the recursion: the emptiness-as-clearance trap was exactly what the 3a review caught and what this gate was written against, and the gate reproduced it one layer down in its own instrument.

detector: state-primitives:ratchet (npm run state-primitives:ratchet, via verify:static)
summary: Bespoke ad-hoc "No X" empty copy regrew past the checked-in ceiling on main twice in one night — 52 (#1665) and again 51 against a ceiling of 50 (#1688, duplicated as #1690) — and the ratchet caught both before any release. A real catch of the regression it exists to prevent, and worth recording for the structural property it exposes rather than the count: a repo-wide count-ratchet fails on whoever gates NEXT, not on whoever caused it. Every branch cutting from main inherited a red completion gate for a reason it did not cause and had to A/B it to prove so, and the path of least resistance under deadline is always to raise the number — which converts a debt signal into permission.
fix_ref: station@008b4ead (#1668) and station@a47a40a3 (#1692) — views ported, ceiling not raised
notes: Recorded as machine-caught because the ratchet genuinely fired on a genuine regrowth. The unattributability is a property of the instrument, not a failure of it — the same shape as the entry-JS bundle budget (#1545, #1112), where each branch measures against a base that does not contain the other in-flight branches.

detector: reading the vitest RUN header and the failing test name instead of the sentinel colour
summary: A fault-injection lane recorded a FAILED sentinel and nearly banked it as a proven guard. The run's first line named a worktree that lane had never touched, and the failing test was one it had never named — its own injection was in an entirely different surface. Vitest without an explicit --root can resolve against a sibling worktree's config while ~20 worktrees are live and 7-13 vitest processes run concurrently. This is a third way an injection lies, alongside the two the delivery protocol already records (a green injection is a finding about your test; a patch that fails to apply surfaces a transform error that reads as a catch): a red can belong to someone else entirely. It satisfies the sentinel, it satisfies a did-it-fail check, and it proves nothing.
evidence_ref: station#1691; RUN header naming station-worktrees/290-flow3-canonical against a lane working elsewhere
notes: Open as a practice change (pin `--root <worktree>` on every vitest invocation and check the RUN line) rather than a code fix. The mirror of vacuous-assertion: there a green meant nothing, here a red means nothing.
